A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, methods, experiments, and theoretical results. The main text and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original membership-inference experiments on image, tabular, and text datasets, including data-scarcity, backbone, defense, and embedding analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and additionally reports truncated-AUC results and full class-drop ROC curves in its appendices.

M1.justification: The conditional-Gaussian quantile-regression implementation, top-two-logit score, attack architectures, and membership-threshold procedure remain unchanged in Sections 2 and 4.

E1.justification: The added plots use existing class-drop experiments on CINIC-10, CIFAR-100, Texas, and 20 Newsgroups. ImageNet scarcity experiments and CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 defense coverage are retained; no new dataset, task, or test scenario is established.

E2.justification: The retained comparisons preserve their named comparators, including LiRA, RMIA, and LOSS. However, the new truncated-AUC comparison in Figure 10 identifies its comparator only as 'Baseline', preventing reliable identification of whether that added comparison introduces a different method.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds AUC truncated at 5% FPR to the existing pointwise TPR and full-AUC evaluation metrics. Previously stated training settings remain unchanged; the new query-size table documents existing experiments without establishing changed sampling.

E4.justification: The score-function ablation, scarcity studies, alternate-backbone tests, defense experiments, and embedding analysis are retained. The added truncated-AUC scores and ROC curves extend benchmark reporting without introducing a distinct ablation, robustness condition, or diagnostic study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, empirical confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new plots do not introduce uncertainty reporting; average query-set sizes are sample-size disclosures.

E6.justification: v3 adds truncated-AUC scores in Figure 10, where QMIA exceeds the displayed 'Baseline', and class-drop ROC curves in Figure 13. Existing result plots, defense-table values, headline TPR comparisons, and Section 5.1 density-ratio fitting errors remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Definitions 5.1–5.2, Theorem 5.3, its assumptions, and its proof are unchanged. The proof moves from Appendix G to H, with only formatting differences.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a new unseen-class auditing setting, failure of shadow-model attacks, stronger quantile-regression performance including up to 11× TPR, and a transferability theorem. The rewritten abstract and introduction retain these contributions and their scope.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly qualifies the motivating CSAM scenario by distinguishing a few query examples potentially available to law enforcement from examples unavailable for attack training. This adds practical applicability detail; the interpretations of shadow-model failure, quantile transferability, and defense results remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds Table 1 with member and nonmember query-set sizes, including 8,979/9,000 for CINIC-10 and 1,245/500 for CIFAR-100 per dropped class or superclass. Hardware, training times, hyperparameters, and existing code-use information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Nasr et al. (2019), Mattern et al. (2023), Shi et al. (2023), and Ye et al. (2022). It distinguishes white-box and generative-text attacks, and prior architecture/procedure mismatch studies, from the paper's setting. These citations are not newly evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the abstract and opening introduction, which foreground safety auditing. v3 also adds an Impact Statement and explanatory cross-references. The technical exposition and main section sequence are largely retained.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column conference formatting, with extensive resizing and rearrangement of figure panels. v3 redisplays the existing CIFAR-100 comparison on the first page and adds the query-size table, truncated-AUC figure, and class-drop ROC figure.

improvement.justification: The query-size table improves transparency about evaluation denominators, while truncated-AUC results and full ROC curves provide additional views of existing experiments. Expanded related work clarifies positioning. These are useful but limited gains: the central evidence and theory are unchanged, and Figure 10 leaves its comparator identity and truncated-AUC normalization insufficiently explained.
